title: API config design draft (routing + rollout)
content:
Purpose:
- Personal scratchpad for API config shape and routing/rollout sketches. Not a final PR.
- Capture ideas for: per-route config, model variant routing, canary/A-B rollout fields, fallback policies, and quick examples for SDK/docs.

Goals:
- Single route config that supports: model pinning, autoscale hints, batching and KV cache TTLs, quantization profile selection, and fallback variants.
- Declarative but extensible: keep core small, allow provider-specific knobs in a freeform section.
- Enable safe rollouts (canary percent, progressive steps, automatic rollback on errors/regressions).

High-level API shape sketch (rough JSON-ish):

route_config: {
  name: string,                      # human name + id derived
  endpoint: string,                  # e.g. /v1/generate-chat
  method: enum("POST","GET"),
  default_model: string,              # primary model id (e.g. redwood/fast-chat-1)
  model_variants: [                   # ordered fallback list / alternatives
    { id: string, weight: int, tags: [string] }
  ],
  rollout: {                          # progressive rollout config
    strategy: enum("immediate","canary","gradual"),
    canary: { percent: int, duration_minutes: int },
    gradual: { steps: [ { percent: int, duration_minutes: int } ] },
    metrics: ["latency_ms", "error_rate", "quality_metric:prompt_set_a"],
    auto_rollback: { enabled: bool, threshold: "error_rate>0.05" }
  },
  routing_policies: [                  # rule-based routing (simple for now)
    { when: "region == 'eu'", model: "redwood/eu-optimized-1" },
    { when: "customer_tier == 'enterprise' && latency_slo_ms < 200", model: "redwood/premium-1" }
  ],
  performance: {                      # hints for infra/runtime
    min_replicas: int,
    max_replicas: int,
    target_latency_ms: int,
    batching: { enabled: bool, max_batch_size: int, max_wait_ms: int },
    kv_cache: { enabled: bool, prefix_ttl_s: int }
  },
  quantization_profile: string,        # e.g. "int8-low-memory" or "float16-high-precision"
  observability: {                     # hooks for tracing and metrics (keep light)
    sampling_rate: float,
    trace_tags: [string]
  },
  freeform: string                     # for provider-specific knobs (e.g. affinity, node selectors)
}

Notes / rationale:
- model_variants: support both weight-based A/B and ordered fallback. For cost-sensitive routes, weights allow mixed serving.
- rollout.metrics: allow user to pick a mix of latency, error, and quality regressions measured by eval prompt sets.
- auto_rollback: must support simple boolean + threshold expr. Implementation can be naive initially (evaluate every minute).

Example request (SDK-friendly):
POST /v1/routes/apply-config
body: { "route_name": "chat-reply", "config": <route_config> }
Response: 202 accepted with deployment id and estimated apply_time.

Example route (concrete):
route_config -> name: "chat-reply", endpoint: "/v1/chat/reply"
- default_model: "redwood/fast-chat-1"
- model_variants: [ {id: "redwood/fast-chat-1", weight: 80}, {id: "redwood/quant-low-1", weight: 20} ]
- rollout: { strategy: "gradual", gradual: [{percent:10,duration_minutes:60},{percent:50,duration_minutes:180}] }
- performance: batching.max_batch_size=64, max_wait_ms=15, kv_cache.enabled=true, prefix_ttl_s=3600

Open questions / TODOs:
- How does per-request override interact with rollout? If a request pins model via header, should it bypass rollout? Probably respect pin but still count toward metrics.
- Gradual rollout murky for stateful sessions (long chat): need to define session affinity semantics (sticky to model variant until conversation end).
- Schema for metrics expressions (simple to start: key op value; later allow time windows).
- UX: Console needs clear visualization for rollout (timeline, error spikes), and ability to pause/rollback manually.

Design tradeoffs:
- Simplicity vs flexibility: prefer simple first-class fields, push complex selection logic to freeform or external policy engine.
- Safety-first: default to conservative rollout (canary 0-10% by default) and require explicit override to immediate.

Sketch: how request routing could flow (simplified ASCII):

  [API request] -> [Auth & Quotas] -> [Route config lookup] -> [Evaluate routing policies] -> [Select model variant via rollout/wts] -> [Enqueue to serving runtime / batcher] -> [Attempt cached prefix hit?] -> [Serve / fallback if model unavailable] -> [Emit metrics]

Implementation notes for runtime team:
- Expose a lightweight API for "select_variant(route, request_meta) -> model_id, variant_meta" that runtime can call synchronously. Keep decision under 5ms.
- Keep rollout state in a small sharded store (per-route) so gradual percentages can be updated without full redeploy.
- Metric collection: tag each request with variant id and rollout cohort so we can compute deltas.

Quick TODOs (for next sync):
- [ ] Write minimal JSON schema for route_config (for use in Console form). (owner: Jamie)
- [ ] Spike: implement in-memory variant selector prototype (owner: Casey). (PR idea: #1345)
- [ ] Draft Console mockups for rollout timeline + manual rollback (owner: Taylor).
- [ ] Align auto_rollback metric definitions with observability team (meeting: INF-312).

References / links:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood/infer/INF-312-config-design
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1345 (initial route-config proto)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime (search "rollout config")

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc informal. Once JSON schema solid, move to shared_drives/product and open a GH draft PR.
- Remember to add examples for function-calling and streaming responses where rollout metrics should capture partial responses.

End of scratchpad.
summary: Personal scratchpad: draft of route_config API for model routing, rollout, and runtime hints. Includes examples, open questions, and next steps.
